what: MCP tool schema design principle (locked in Apr 21 2026): every new MCP tool parameter in src/memory/server.ts must tolerate LLM output quirks EXCEPT enum values, which stay strict. Specifically: numbers accept string form via `z.coerce.number()`; arrays accept single-item shortcuts via the `lenientArray()` helper; booleans accept string "true"/"false"/"1"/"0" via `lenientBoolean`; every optional field uses `.nullish().transform((v) => v ?? undefined)` to accept both null and undefined. Enums intentionally reject unknown values (prevents silent bad-data storage — if the LLM mistypes "tech" for "technical", we want the error loud, not silent). When adding a new MCP tool: grep existing tools for the same input shape, copy the schema pattern, add a regression test in src/memory/__tests__/server.test.ts that exercises the lenient path. All 660 tests + the 6 lenient-regression tests lock this in.
why: Forward-looking guardrail for anyone touching server.ts (adding a new MCP tool, extending an existing one). Every lenient pattern has a regression test. Without this captured as a guideline, the next tool added is likely to revert to strict zod defaults and break agent tool-calls the same way aide_forget did today.
